experimentContext: Compare the user's normal signed-in marketplace contexts with the anonymous restaurant-direct flow for one overlapping scheduled pickup window.
tipPolicy: Set optional pickup tips to $0 before recording a final checkout total.
comparisonStatus: Uber Eats was $1.53 cheaper than DoorDash for one equivalent Sarge's basket. Toast displayed a lower provisional total but was excluded because its disclosed card surcharge remained unresolved without a payment method.
limitations: The restaurant was closed for immediate online ordering, so every channel was configured for a scheduled pickup. The two exact marketplace windows overlapped from 10:30 AM through 10:50 AM.
This is one basket at one restaurant on one date, not evidence of a persistent cheapest channel.
Uber Eats and DoorDash were signed in while Toast was anonymous because those were the user's normal available paths; account context is recorded per observation.

Toast disclosed a 3% credit-card surcharge but showed it as $0.00 before a payment method was selected. Its $30.43 displayed total is therefore not a final payable quote and was excluded from the winner.

The 838-second end-to-end time includes source navigation, first-time scheduled-pickup workflow discovery, the incomplete Toast investigation, and correcting DoorDash from delivery to pickup before the accepted quote.
Both exact totals and their pickup windows were immediately rechecked. All temporary carts were cleared and no order was placed.
